findings: Q1 SEAL MECHANICS (eaten-path): The seal is NOT a physics collider. Movement is projection onto the corridor polyline as continuous (s, lat); the seal is a one-line parametric clamp: C:/Users/Alex/Projects/eaten-path/src/world.js:295 `if (this.sealPoint.seg === seg) s = Math.max(s, this.sealPoint.s + 2.2)` — a guaranteed 2.2 m clearance that can only push the player FORWARD along always-walkable path (children pre-spawn 48 m ahead, LOOKAHEAD world.js:11,320). Seal trees are pure visuals and never enter seg.colliders (colliders are only props, world.js:304-314), so no physics deadlock is possible.

Q1 WHY THE PLAYER CAN NEVER BE CAUGHT: (a) the frontier is defined RELATIVE to the player every frame — target = sCur - SEAL_TRAIL(12 m), world.js:359 — and its authored pressure floors are 7 m (idle >40 s, world.js:361) and 5 m (forwardUrge herding, world.js:363-365), all far above the 2.2 m clamp, so the frontier can never reach the player on its own; only walking backwards touches it. (b) the advance is rate-limited to max(1.5, gap*2.4) m/s (world.js:367). (c) crucially, project() returns FRACTIONAL s (nearest sample then refinement against adjacent polyline edges, world.js:204-219) and pointAt() interpolates fractional s (world.js:229-241), so the clamp resolves to a position that exactly satisfies itself — it fires once and quiesces, and any forward input increases s continuously past it.

Q1 COMMIT GRAMMAR: forks; walking COMMIT_S=6 m into a branch permanently seals the parent + all siblings (world.js:292, _commit 324-346): dense instant-ish wall across each rejected mouth (6 m at 1.1 m spacing, world.js:332), parent tail closes in a rush back to the fork (world.js:338-341), then sealPoint jumps to sCur-12. Fork throat deadlock is explicitly guarded: mouth-of-branch projection matches are penalized EXCEPT when pressed against the current segment's end (world.js:270-274 'otherwise the fork throat deadlocks at walk speed').

Q2 WITNESSING THE SEAL: (1) Taught at second zero — begin() spawns an INSTANT seal wall right behind the spawn point ('the tape starts with the way back already gone', world.js:93-96), so the very first look back shows the mechanic. (2) Commit = a loud spatialized sealRush AT the fork you just left, 6 m behind, with audio ducking (events.js:26-31, audio.js:444-449) — an unmistakable turn-around cue. (3) A 4.5 s sealLookWindow: if the camera then faces the seal point (dot>0.55, <28 m) you get a sub-bass sealSting payoff (events.js:636-645, audio.js:451-458) — looking back is authored and rewarded. (4) Continuous pressure: every frontier spawn triggers sealCreak on a 2.2-4.5 s cooldown (events.js:32-37, audio.js:442). (5) The rise is SLOW enough to catch: trunks rise 1.9-3 s with 0-0.5 s stagger, shrubs 1.6 s (flora.js:428,439,483-499) — a glance back sees motion, not a fait accompli. (6) Geometry forces turns: per-biome kink 0.22-0.52 curves the path (world.js:15-23), fork mouths pinch like doorways (halfWidthAt world.js:249-251), and signposts at forks make you stop and read while the parent seals (flora.js:444-481). (7) Balking herds you: forwardUrge closes the forest audibly behind you with whispers (events.js:612-620 + world.js:363-365).

Q3 FOREST LOOK ON A BUDGET (eaten-path): All vegetation is exact-count InstancedMesh baked once per segment from a plan (flora.js:280-335) — 4 shared geometries (cylinder trunk, squashed icosahedron canopy, cross-plane alphaTest shrub, torus root) + per-instance setColorAt tint jitter (flora.js:298-312) to kill repetition. Distribution: exponential falloff from the corridor edge `off = halfW + 0.7 + -log(1-u)*(spread*0.45)` capped (flora.js:137) → a dense tree WALL at the path edge thinning outward; near-wall trunks LEAN over the path (flora.js:141). Sky closure: overhead canopy blobs at 3.2-7.4 m over the path (flora.js:167-175) + knitting branches spanning it (177-183). Corridor surface: shrub walls every ~1 m using un-pinched width so foliage never presses the lens at mouths (flora.js:186-199). Ground: two vertex-colored ribbons — a wide +7.5 m fringe with per-vertex tint jitter (232-272) and a raised pale trail ribbon (0.72*halfW, cap 1.5 m) with wheel-rut canvas texture (273-277, 41-47) for path readability. Atmosphere: per-biome FogExp2 color+density smoothly damped, fog color == scene.background so the 80 m far plane reads intentional (main.js:29-43, 211-215); light comes FROM the camera (camcorder spotlight intensity 220 + near fill, main.js:53-62) over a starved ambient/hemi/moon base (46-52), plus dust motes in the beam (72-91). Variety is rationed: landmark biomes with starvation guards force a set-piece every 3-5 segments (world.js:113-124); additive sun shafts + ground discs (flora.js:337-349). Zero texture assets — everything canvasTexture speckle (flora.js:36-56).

Q4 THE EXACT PIN DEFECT IN FETCH (C:/Users/Alex/Projects/fetch-claude/src/outside.js): project() returns an INTEGER sample index — `return { s: best, ... }` at outside.js:262 with no edge refinement — and both posAt() (line 266 `Math.round(s)`) and the seal push (lines 289-295 `this.samples[clamp(Math.round(s), ...)]`) quantize to whole samples, while sealS advances in float increments (line 307). Pin sequence: player backs into the frontier (walkers spawn BEHIND the player at director.js:379-385, and the arena at outside.js:207 makes retreating natural) → pr.s < minS = sealS+2.2 → push snaps pos to sample k = round(minS). Whenever frac(sealS+2.2) < 0.5 (a coin flip), k < minS, so the pushed position STILL violates the clamp. Every subsequent frame: _moveAxis moves ≤ ~0.08 m, project() re-quantizes to the same integer k, the push re-fires and rewrites pos purely as `sm + perp*lat` (no along-track term) — erasing ALL forward progress. Escape forward needs >0.5 m in one frame (impossible at 4.7 m/s); lateral escape is capped by the lat clamp at halfW-0.38 ≈ 1.1 m, far below the halfW+3 jurisdiction release (lines 276-277). Result: permanently locked, cannot move any direction — exactly Alex's report (docs/PLAYTEST-3.md item 8).

Q4 MINIMAL FIX: make the seal clamp continuous, as eaten-path does. (1) In Forest.project (outside.js:242-263): after finding the best integer index, refine against the two adjacent polyline edges (project onto segments [best-1,best] and [best,best+1], t clamped 0..1, keep closest) and return fractional s — the exact algorithm at eaten-path world.js:210-219. (2) In posAt (outside.js:265-269): interpolate between floor(s) and floor(s)+1 instead of Math.round — eaten-path pointAt world.js:229-241. (3) In clampPlayer's push (outside.js:289-295): compute s = Math.max(pr.s, minS) and place via the fractional posAt, so the post-push position satisfies s >= minS, the clamp self-quiesces next frame, and forward input always escapes. Three small edits; no feel-core files touched.

Q4 SECONDARY TRAP (same file family): dying in the forest respawns at the gate (director.js:526-538 → teleport('forest'), spawn at director.js:13) but main.js:358-362 only resets forest.sealS/_lastIdx/entered when act is NOT forest/clearing/cave — so after a forest death the player spawns ~s=3 BEHIND a frontier that may be at s=90, with a stale ±40 warm-start window (outside.js:245) whose cold-rescan guard (line 252) never fires because _lastIdx is mid-range. The forest silently ignores them until they physically near the stale window, then the seal push teleports them up to ~80 m forward (or pins them per the integer bug). Fix: on teleport to act==='forest', also reset _lastIdx=0, sealS=-10, entered=false (or sealS = max(-10, respawn s - SEAL_TRAIL)).

Q4 WHY THE SEAL IS NEVER WITNESSED IN FETCH: _placeSeal (outside.js:391-410) re-seeds ONE 48-instance pool, repositioning ALL 48 trunks every 2.5 m of frontier advance — so the wall exists only at the frontier (~6 sparse rows) and the already-sealed corridor behind it is left visibly EMPTY (old trunks teleport away); the only cue is a reused brushCrash (line 409). There is no instant wall at the gate on entry, no commit/rush moment, no creak loop, no look-back reward, and the frontier trails a constant 10 m with no herding — so nothing ever asks the player to turn around, and if they do they see a thin, teleporting picket line instead of a forest that ate the path.

summary: Eaten-path's seal is safe because it is not physics: the player's position is a continuous (s, lat) coordinate on the corridor spline, and the seal is a one-way clamp s = max(s, sealPoint.s + 2.2) (world.js:295) whose frontier only chases player-relative floors (12/7/5 m) — it can only ever push you forward onto path that always exists, and the fractional projection means the clamp self-quiesces after one push. FETCH ported the pattern but quantized it: project() returns integer sample indices and the push rounds to whole samples (outside.js:262, 266, 289-295), so when frac(sealS+2.2) < 0.5 the push lands on a sample that still violates the clamp and re-fires every frame, erasing all movement — a permanent all-directions pin, matching Alex's report exactly. Minimal fix is three edits porting eaten-path's fractional refinement into project/posAt/the push; a secondary trap (forest-death respawn keeps a deep sealS, main.js:358-362) needs a reset. The seal was never witnessed because FETCH recycles one 48-trunk pool at the frontier (empty corridor behind, one reused sound) and never asks for a look back; eaten-path's donor kit — instant gate wall at entry, cumulative seal pool, 2-3 s staggered rises, creak loop + rush + look-back sting, and idle-creep herding — plus its cheap look stack (exponential tree falloff with lean, shrub walls, overhead canopy, two-ribbon ground, fog-matched background, camera-borne light) are all directly portable into outside.js without touching the feel core.
